newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Foreign inflows into Brazil bolsas slow in March.
newsitem.headline: Foreign inflows into Brazil bolsas slow in March.

text.p: Figures from Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM) showed that net foreign capital inflows into the country reached $599.3 million, primarily going into the stock market.
The money was invested under Annex Four rules which regulate foreign investment in Brazil's stock market, securities and debentures.
In February, net foreign investment into Brazilian bourses amounted to $749 million.
Foreign capital inflows totalled $1.8 billion in March, with outflows at $1.2 billion, CVM reported.
In the first quarter, net foreign capital inflows totalled $2.3 billion, it said.
Foreign capital inflows exceeded outflows by $15 billion last year in Brazil under Annex Four rules, it added.
